title: Burst config schema draft (Dedicated) — tenant enablement, limits, defaulting
body:
Last updated: 2025-06-15 (Benji)

Context
- We need a config surface to enable “burst capacity” for Dedicated tenants and define guardrails (hard limits + cooldowns + pool eligibility).
- This is intended to live in the control plane and be evaluated by burst-policy-service (ENG-4823). Routing consumes an admission result (ENG-4824) and will not “self-decide” eligibility.
- Design goals:
  1) Safe defaults: burst is off unless explicitly enabled.
  2) Deterministic evaluation: given (tenant, region, gpu_type, time, request) → stable decision.
  3) Minimize cardinality explosion: avoid per-model/per-route overrides as a first-class default; allow controlled scoping.
  4) Easy ops: can be disabled per-tenant quickly (global kill switch + per-tenant override).

Non-goals for this schema (v1)
- Customer-managed burst pools.
- Cross-region burst by default (we allow “same region only” in v1; cross-region requires explicit allow + routing semantics review).
- Preemption knobs (v1 is strict admission control, not eviction policy).

Key objects
We likely need:
- A top-level “BurstPolicyConfig” (global defaults + safety kill switch)
- Per-tenant “TenantBurstConfig” (enablement + limits + pool eligibility)
- Optional per-region overrides (same tenant)

Naming note
I’m using “burst” consistently; avoid “overflow”/“shared-headroom” synonyms in schema fields.

========================
Proposed schema (logical)
========================

1) Global config (control-plane)

BurstPolicyConfig
- version: string (schema version, not feature version)
- global_enabled: bool
  - emergency kill switch; if false, all admissions denied with reason=BurstGloballyDisabled
- evaluation_cache_ttl_seconds: int
  - policy-engine caching (see determinism concerns + invalidation plan)
- default_tenant_policy: TenantBurstConfigDefaults
  - applied when tenant has no explicit config (but burst should still be disabled unless allowlist says otherwise)
- default_limit_profile: BurstLimitProfile
  - safe default numbers used when a tenant is enabled but omits a field
- validation:
  - global_enabled default = true (feature flag still gates rollout), BUT admission must still require tenant enablement.

TenantBurstConfigDefaults
- burst_enabled_default: bool (default false)
- allow_burst_pools_default: list[string] (default empty)

2) Tenant config (primary)

TenantBurstConfig
- tenant_id: string (canonical Redwood tenant/org id)
- enabled: bool (default false)
- mode: string enum ["deny_by_default", "allow_by_default"]
  - v1: hardcode/validate mode="deny_by_default" unless we decide to support allow-by-default for internal tenants.
- allow_pools: list[string]
  - explicit pool ids or pool selectors (see PoolSelector below). Default empty.
- allow_regions: list[string]
  - e.g. ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]. Default empty.
- allow_gpu_types: list[string]
  - e.g. ["h100", "a100"]. Default empty.
- cross_region_fallback_allowed: bool (default false)
- limits: BurstLimitProfile
- cooldowns: BurstCooldownPolicy
- windows: BurstTimeWindows
  - optional schedule constraints (e.g. allow burst during business hours / batch windows)
- metering: BurstMeteringPolicy
- audit: AuditAnnotations
  - not for authz; purely annotation fields for traceability.

PoolSelector (optional but recommended direction)
- type: enum ["pool_id", "label_selector"]
- value: string
  - pool_id: exact match (e.g. "burst/us-east-1/h100/pool-03")
  - label_selector: simple expression (e.g. "region=us-east-1,gpu=h100,tier=burst")

3) Limit profile

BurstLimitProfile
- max_concurrent_requests: int
  - Hard cap for admitted concurrent requests routed into burst pools.
- max_requests_per_second: float
  - Admission gate; if exceeded, deny with reason=BurstTenantRpsLimit.
- max_tokens_per_second: float
  - Admission gate; token rate estimated from recent usage / declared prompt+max_tokens.
- max_queue_depth: int
  - If we introduce queueing on burst pools (future), cap backlog.
- max_burst_fraction_of_baseline: float
  - Optional safety: (burst_tps <= baseline_tps * fraction). Default null/0 in v1 unless we want it.
- per_model_overrides: string
  - v1: store as opaque JSON string (if we must) or disallow entirely.
  - Recommendation: disallow for beta; keep schema slot for future.

Validation rules (tenant)
- If enabled=true:
  - allow_pools OR (allow_regions + allow_gpu_types) must be non-empty.
  - At least one of: max_concurrent_requests, max_requests_per_second, max_tokens_per_second must be set (otherwise too risky).
- max_* must be >= 0. Values of 0 mean “deny all burst” (useful as a quick per-tenant off without flipping enabled).
- cross_region_fallback_allowed requires allow_regions length > 1 (or explicit “fallback_region_allowlist”).

4) Cooldowns / backoff

BurstCooldownPolicy
- deny_cooldown_seconds: int
  - After a deny due to saturation or tenant limit, apply cooldown to avoid hammering policy/routing.
- admit_cooldown_seconds: int
  - Optional; rate-limit transitions / avoid thrash.
- burst_session_max_seconds: int
  - Upper bound for how long we keep a tenant in “bursting” state before requiring re-authorization.
- circuit_breaker:
  - global_pool_saturation_gate: float (0..1)
  - per_pool_saturation_gate: float (0..1)
  - neighbor_p99_drift_gate_ms: int

NOTE: circuit_breaker settings might be global-only (SRE-owned). If so, we keep it out of TenantBurstConfig and expose only “respect_circuit_breakers=true/false” (default true, cannot be disabled for external tenants).

5) Time windows

BurstTimeWindows
- timezone: string (IANA tz name, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles")
- allowed_windows: list[Window]
- denied_windows: list[Window]

Window
- days: string (e.g. "Mon-Fri" or "Sat,Sun")
- start: string ("HH:MM")
- end: string ("HH:MM")

Precedence
- denied_windows take precedence over allowed_windows.
- If allowed_windows empty → allow all times (subject to other gates).

6) Metering

BurstMeteringPolicy
- shadow_metering_enabled: bool (default true for beta)
- usage_attribution_tag: string
  - e.g. "burst" vs "baseline"; used by billing pipeline.
- emit_customer_visible_metrics: bool (default true)
- include_reason_codes_in_headers: bool (default true, but must be safelisted codes)

7) Audit annotations

AuditAnnotations
- change_ticket: string (e.g. "INT-881" or "ENG-4822")
- owner_team: string (e.g. "dedicated-platform")
- notes: string

========================
Defaulting & inheritance
========================

Overall approach
- Global config provides only defaults.
- Tenant must have enabled=true to burst (no implicit enablement).
- Tenant config can include “regional_overrides” but we should keep it limited.

Proposed precedence order (highest wins)
1. Emergency controls (global kill switch, pool gates, circuit breakers)
2. Tenant explicit config (TenantBurstConfig)
3. Tenant regional override (if we add it; or make it part of TenantBurstConfig keyed by region)
4. Global default_limit_profile

Field-level defaulting rules
- enabled: default false
- allow_pools: default []
- allow_regions: default []
- allow_gpu_types: default []
- limits.max_concurrent_requests: default 0 unless explicitly set? (safer)
  - Recommendation: if enabled=true and max_concurrent_requests omitted, default to a conservative number (e.g. 10) so customers aren’t forced to set it, but we’re not “unlimited”.
- cooldowns.deny_cooldown_seconds: default 30
- cross_region_fallback_allowed: default false
- windows.timezone: default "UTC"
- metering.shadow_metering_enabled: default true for beta

Open question: Should we allow “enabled=true” with no limits, relying purely on pool circuit breakers?
- My take: no. Needs tenant-level hard cap.

========================
Example configs
========================

A) Minimal tenant enablement (JSON)

{
  "tenant_id": "tn_8f3c2b1a",
  "enabled": true,
  "allow_regions": ["us-east-1"],
  "allow_gpu_types": ["h100"],
  "limits": {
    "max_concurrent_requests": 40,
    "max_tokens_per_second": 120000
  },
  "cooldowns": {
    "deny_cooldown_seconds": 30,
    "burst_session_max_seconds": 900
  },
  "metering": {
    "shadow_metering_enabled": true,
    "usage_attribution_tag": "burst",
    "emit_customer_visible_metrics": true,
    "include_reason_codes_in_headers": true
  },
  "audit": {
    "change_ticket": "Linear:ENG-4822",
    "owner_team": "dedicated-platform",
    "notes": "Beta enablement for design partner; strict caps; us-east-1 only"
  }
}

B) Explicit pool allowlist + time windows (YAML)

tenant_id: tn_2b7f9d11
enabled: true
allow_pools:
  - type: pool_id
    value: burst/us-east-1/h100/pool-03
  - type: pool_id
    value: burst/us-east-1/h100/pool-04
limits:
  max_concurrent_requests: 25
  max_requests_per_second: 60
  max_tokens_per_second: 80000
cooldowns:
  deny_cooldown_seconds: 45
  admit_cooldown_seconds: 5
  burst_session_max_seconds: 1200
windows:
  timezone: America/Los_Angeles
  allowed_windows:
    - days: Mon-Fri
      start: "08:00"
      end: "18:00"
  denied_windows:
    - days: Sat,Sun
      start: "00:00"
      end: "23:59"
metering:
  shadow_metering_enabled: true
  usage_attribution_tag: burst
  emit_customer_visible_metrics: true
  include_reason_codes_in_headers: true

C) “Disable quickly” pattern (keep enabled but set limit=0)

{
  "tenant_id": "tn_8f3c2b1a",
  "enabled": true,
  "allow_regions": ["us-east-1"],
  "allow_gpu_types": ["h100"],
  "limits": {
    "max_concurrent_requests": 0
  },
  "audit": {
    "change_ticket": "INT-881",
    "notes": "Temporarily disable burst without removing config; incident mitigation"
  }
}

========================
Admission decision reason codes (for headers/logs)
========================

We should standardize these now so we don’t leak internal detail later.
Suggested enum values (safe to expose):
- BurstGloballyDisabled
- BurstTenantDisabled
- BurstOutsideAllowedWindow
- BurstRegionNotAllowed
- BurstGpuTypeNotAllowed
- BurstPoolNotEligible
- BurstTenantConcurrencyLimit
- BurstTenantRpsLimit
- BurstTenantTpsLimit
- BurstPoolSaturated
- BurstCircuitBreakerOpen
- BurstPolicyError

Routing mapping guidance (not schema, but impacts schema expectations)
- If denied due to tenant config → return 429 with reason in header
- If denied due to pool saturation / circuit breaker → likely 503 with retry-after + reason
(Need final decision from routing/SRE; this doc is just flagging it.)

========================
Validation / safety checks
========================

Control plane validation (write-time)
- Disallow enabled=true if no allow_* set.
- Enforce max_* upper bounds (to avoid fat-finger “1200000” vs “120000”).
  - Proposed max caps (beta):
    - max_concurrent_requests <= 500
    - max_requests_per_second <= 2000
    - max_tokens_per_second <= 500000
- Ensure timezone is valid IANA.
- Ensure windows are non-overlapping? (Optional; at least validate formatting.)

Policy engine enforcement (read-time)
- If global_enabled=false → deny.
- If circuit breaker open → deny.
- If tenant enabled=false → deny.
- If outside allowed windows → deny.
- If pool selection yields 0 eligible pools → deny.
- Apply tenant limits.

========================
Open questions / TODO
========================

1) Do we want region overrides inside a single tenant object?
Option A: TenantBurstConfig.regional_overrides: map[region]TenantBurstConfigPartial
Option B: Separate objects keyed by (tenant_id, region)
- A is simpler for customers; B is cleaner for storage/indexing.

2) Pool selection semantics
- If allow_pools specified: should that override allow_regions/allow_gpu_types?
- My recommendation: allow_pools is authoritative; allow_regions/gpu_types are ignored (or must be consistent).

3) Limit units & estimation
- tokens_per_second depends on estimation. Need to confirm with Telemetry team how we compute / what data-plane signal exists at admission time.

4) How to represent per-model overrides safely
- Probably do NOT ship in beta.
- If we need it internally, keep a separate internal-only config (not customer-facing) or a “debug_overrides_json” string that is gated.

5) Kill switch ownership
- global_enabled should be SRE-owned; restrict write access (RBAC).

========================
Next steps
========================
- Get agreement from Ethan/Jordan on object model + validation (ENG-4822/4823).
- Confirm with Mina (routing) which deny reason codes need to be surfaced vs kept internal.
- Align with Cole/Nadia on metering fields (shadow metering tags) so we don’t redo later.

Notes to self
- Keep this schema boring. The real complexity belongs in policy evaluation + circuit breakers, not customer config.
- Don’t expose per-pool weights in v1 unless fleet insists; it’s hard to explain and easy to misuse.
